The competent General, territorial, diocesan, religious, parish and church calendar, the approved books and the competent annual Ordo control an actual celebration. Verify against a dated official witness before relying on any date, and never cite this file as an occurrence witness.

precedence.note: No general table of precedence is stated in guidance/liturgy/calendar-computation.md, so a date carrying more than one candidate lists them all unranked, temporal candidates before fixed-date ones. The `rank` a candidate carries is the rank its own calendar prints, not a computed ordering, and it does not resolve the day. The competent Ordo decides which mass is said. `appointed` is the one exception, and it states no precedence either: a commemoration is not a rival mass but a text said within the mass of the day, so setting the commemorations aside reads what the index records rather than ordering what it does not. Where more than one mass remains after that, `appointed` is null.

missals.edition_qualification: Declared typical on 23 June 1962 (Novo rubricarum corpore). The reader's Canon includes Saint Joseph's name, inserted by the decree of 13 November 1962 (in force 8 December 1962; AAS 54 [1962] 873), a variation within the same edition. Coverage is partial: each body keeps its own witness and rights evidence, and finding-aid, OCR-only and placeholder regions remain.

missals.edition: Roman Missal, 2002 third typical edition, 2008 emended reprint
missals.edition_qualification: The 2008 corrected reprint of the third typical edition, expressly not a new typical edition (Prot. 652/08/L). The reader's calendar also carries later decreed inscriptions recorded in the source, such as Mary, Mother of the Church (2018). No copy of the 2008 altar book is held: Latin bodies come from identified sources and only some are attested to the target, and English is historical or project-study translation, not the approved 2011 text.

The reader holds this edition as it stood before the 1955 simplification of the rubrics and the restored Holy Week, as witnessed by the Bonn 2004 reprint of the 28th edition conformed to the Vatican typical edition (a printing of about 1954); no authenticated Vatican 1920 impression is held. Only three Pentecost prayers are collated to that witness; its Holy Week departures and two sanctoral absences are established, other Proper wording is inherited uncollated from the 1962 typical edition, the Ordinary comes from an 1861 lay missal, and precedence is a linearized finding aid.

structure/rubrics/index.json.advisory: A finding aid for how a day is put together, and never an authority for what was celebrated. The rules here are transcribed from this repository's own collated publications; the competent particular calendar, a legitimate indult and the competent annual Ordo control an actual celebration. Precedence is one of five decisions, and this layer takes only that one and the orations that follow from it.
